Sally — thanks for sending. Short answer: video-notary / tele-witnessing is acceptable in most cases, provided certain verification artifacts are present. Below is a concise checklist we use to validate EIN + signer authority so Procurement can release the PO: 

Redwood EIN & W-9 remote verification checklist:
- Signed W-9 (wet signature or DocuSign) with printed name and title visible.
- EIN evidence: one of the following — (a) bank letter on bank letterhead referencing the business name and EIN, (b) IRS CP 575/CP 575/other official IRS issuance (screenshot acceptable if from IRS portal), or (c) notarized affidavit referencing EIN.
- If using tele-notary/video witnessing: include a time-stamped recording or notarization certificate that references the witness method and the notary's commission number.
- Photo ID of the signer (driver's license or passport) and a short liveness check (video clip or still + timestamp).
- Clear signer authority: either a corporate officer title on the W-9 or a signed corporate resolution/authorization PDF.

Logistics / options we support:
- DocuSign envelope + embedded ID verification (fastest). Please share the envelope link and we can accept the audit trail.
- Tele-notary recording + notarization certificate (we'll accept a recording + notarization PDF).
- Physical notarization if tele-notary is not an option.

Cc'ing Naomi (procurement ops) so she can map the checklist to the PO gating steps and give a target activation date once we have the artifacts. If you can return the signed W-9 and the bank letter (preferably notarized or tele-notary with certificate), we can start a provisional PO flow while final verification completes.

Action items for Sage Systems:
- Return signed W-9 (PDF) via DocuSign or email.
- Submit bank letter with one of the acceptable evidences above.
- Include signer photo ID (redact SSN) and indicate signer title.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

Best,

Hi all — reviewing the attachments now. Thanks for the quick turnaround, Sally. The DocuSign audit trail and the tele-notary certificate look sufficient for our standard PO activation. Two short notes from Procurement: 

1) For formal PO issuance we require one of the following to perform final EIN reconciliation:
   - IRS CP 575 or a PDF screenshot from the IRS EIN confirmation page showing the company name and EIN, OR
   - A bank letter (on bank letterhead) that explicitly states the EIN, or
   - A notarized affidavit referencing the EIN (we'll accept tele-notary + certificate as you provided).

2) The W-9 you provided looks complete; please redact any SSN/TIN portion if it's sensitive in email, but keep the full copy in DocuSign.

Next steps and expected timelines:
- If you can confirm you will provide either the IRS confirmation (screenshot/PDF) or the unredacted bank letter to Procurement by EOD Wed (29 Jul), we will schedule PO issuance the following business day.
- In the interim, we can create a provisional PO (PO-0007842-PROV) to allow procurement engineering to provision account access and test billing routing (no funds will disburse until final verification).

Sally — please upload any large recordings to a secure share (we provided a secure upload link in the DocuSign envelope) or confirm that the tele-notary provider can transfer the certificate directly to procurement@redwood.com. 

I'll mark this thread as the official PO gating thread and will follow up if anything else comes up. Logan / Naomi — flagging for procurement queue.
